iut_type: Referencing multiple existing QDIDs with overlapping layer coverage triggers new lower-layer test requirements -- simplification strategy when the overlapping layers' ICS content is actually identical
customer_question: We want our new registration to reference two existing QDIDs: a Controller-level QDID and a broader Component QDID (covering RF PHY through SM) from the same chip vendor. Since these two QDIDs overlap in their RF PHY and Link Layer coverage, does this combination require additional testing, and can it be avoided?
question_variants: Why would referencing two existing, already-certified QDIDs together ever trigger new test requirements?
If two QDIDs' overlapping layers are identical, is there any reason to reference both rather than just the broader one?
actual_issue: The customer wanted their new registration to reference both a narrower Controller-level QDID and a broader Component-level QDID from the same chip vendor, where the two QDIDs' RF PHY and Link Layer (LL) coverage overlapped -- and discovered that combining them this way, while technically permitted under the post-July-2024 registration system, would trigger new lower-layer protocol test requirements that could not be satisfied using the chip vendor's own existing module-registration test reports.
plain_english_explanation: Since July 1, 2024, the registration site allows selecting overlapping/duplicate layers across multiple referenced QDIDs, but doing so causes the system's Test Plan to generate new lower-layer protocol test requirements. This happens because the required test items are governed by the current, latest specification content -- and the chip vendor's own pre-existing test report (created when those QDIDs were originally registered, potentially under older specification content) will be missing some of the now-required newest test items, making it insufficient as evidence. However, in this case, comparing all the layers in question across the narrower Controller QDID, the broader Component QDID, and a third related reference showed that the RF PHY and LL layer ICS content was actually IDENTICAL across all of them. This meant that simply referencing ONLY the broader Component QDID (which already fully covers the same RF PHY and LL content the narrower QDID would have added) produces the exact same resulting ICS, with no additional test requirement at all -- as long as the customer doesn't specifically need to preserve a visible reference trail to the narrower QDID in the registration for some other (non-technical) reason, such as wanting that specific reference to appear in the registration record.
consultant_answer: Referencing both QDIDs together, since they overlap in RF PHY and LL coverage, would trigger new lower-layer protocol test requirements under the current system -- and the chip vendor's existing test report from when those QDIDs were originally registered won't have all the now-required latest test items, so it can't be used as evidence. However, we compared the actual ICS content across both QDIDs (and a third related one) and found the RF PHY and LL layers are identical across all of them -- so you can simply reference only the broader Component QDID and get the exact same resulting ICS with no additional testing required, unless you specifically want the narrower QDID's reference to remain visible in the registration for some other reason.
decision_logic: When a customer wants to reference multiple existing QDIDs whose layer coverage overlaps, check whether the overlapping layers' actual ICS content is identical across all referenced QDIDs -- if so, recommend referencing only the broadest/most complete QDID to achieve the same resulting registration scope without triggering the new lower-layer test requirements that combining overlapping references would otherwise cause.
final_recommendation: Before finalizing a multi-QDID reference structure with overlapping layer coverage, compare the actual ICS content of the overlapping layers across all candidate QDIDs -- if identical, recommend simplifying to a single, broader reference to avoid unnecessary new test requirements and reduce registration support cost, reserving the multi-reference structure only for cases where the customer has a specific non-technical reason to preserve a visible reference trail.
risk_if_done_wrong: Referencing multiple overlapping QDIDs without checking for ICS content identity could result in unexpected new lower-layer test requirements that the chip vendor's existing test reports can't satisfy, adding unnecessary cost and delay to a registration that could have been completed without any additional testing.
